cards.back: An **engineering discipline** concerned with **all aspects of software production**, from early specification through to maintenance after the system goes into use.
The **programs + all associated documentation + configuration data** needed to make the programs work correctly. Not just code.

cards.front: Four essential attributes of good software
cards.back: **Maintainability**, **Dependability & security**, **Efficiency**, **Acceptability**.

Coined at the **1968 NATO conference**. As hardware grew, ad-hoc methods couldn't build/maintain growing-complexity software → projects over budget, over time, low quality, unmaintainable. SE = the disciplined response.
**F**unctionality, **L**ocalizability, **U**sability, **R**eliability, **P**erformance, **S**upportability — a checklist of software quality dimensions (variant of FURPS).
**Generic** = sold to anyone on the open market; developer controls the spec (e.g. Word). **Bespoke** = commissioned by one customer who controls the spec (e.g. ATC system).

A **faulty content/config update** crashed a **kernel-level driver** → BSOD boot-loops on ~8.5M machines. NOT a hack. Lessons: **test content updates**, **staged/canary rollout**, **defensive/fault-tolerant design**, **rollback** path.
**Specification** (what), **Development** (design & implement), **Validation** (check it), **Evolution** (change it). Present in every process model.
Use when **requirements are stable & well-understood**. Plan-driven, document-driven, sequential. Weakness: **inflexible to change**; working software appears **late**.
Each **build phase is paired with a test level** (reqs↔acceptance, system design↔system test, arch design↔integration, module↔unit). Tests are designed **early**, in parallel with development.
**Risk-driven**, iterative loops: (1) determine objectives → (2) **identify & resolve risks** → (3) develop & test → (4) plan next iteration. Suits large, costly, high-risk projects.
**Incremental** = deliver the system in complete *slices* over time. **Iterative** = build a rough *whole*, then refine over repeated passes. Agile is **both**.
**Investigation → Analysis → Design → Implementation → Maintenance**, each adding a security activity. Big idea = **'shift security left'** (catch flaws early).
**People → Product → Process → Project**. **People** are the most important asset. (Pressman.)
**Product Life Cycle** (market: intro→growth→maturity→decline) ⊃ **PMLC** (initiate→plan→execute→monitor→close) ⊃ **SDLC** (the engineering process).

**Individuals & interactions** > processes/tools · **Working software** > documentation · **Customer collaboration** > contract negotiation · **Responding to change** > following a plan. (Value the LEFT more.)
**Product Owner** (prioritises backlog, voice of customer), **Scrum Master** (servant-leader/facilitator, removes impediments), **Development Team** (cross-functional, self-organising, builds it).
**Product Backlog** (ordered master list), **Sprint Backlog** (items committed this sprint + plan), **Increment** (potentially shippable 'Done' product).
**Sprint Planning** (pick work), **Daily Scrum** (~15-min sync), **Sprint Review** (demo product → feedback), **Sprint Retrospective** (improve team/process).
**Review** inspects the **product** (did we build the right thing? demo to stakeholders). **Retrospective** inspects the **team/process** (how do we improve?).
**'As a `<user>`, I want `<goal>`, so that `<benefit>`.'** The 3 C's: **Card** (the story), **Conversation** (the detail), **Confirmation** (acceptance criteria).
**I**ndependent, **N**egotiable, **V**aluable, **E**stimable, **S**mall, **T**estable.

**TDD** = write the failing test *first*, then code to pass. **Pair programming** = two devs, one machine (continuous review). **Refactoring** = improve internal structure, **same external behaviour**.
**Maximise customer value, minimise waste.** 7 principles incl. eliminate waste, amplify learning, decide late, deliver fast, empower team, build integrity in, see the whole. **Kanban** limits WIP.
**User** = abstract natural-language statements for customers (what they want). **System** = detailed, structured specification for developers (the contract to implement).
**Elicitation** (discover) → **Analysis & negotiation** (classify, resolve conflicts) → **Specification** (write the SRS) → **Validation** (check it's right). Plus ongoing **management**.
**Active** (analyst drives): interviews, workshops/JAD, brainstorming, prototyping. **Passive** (analyst observes): **ethnography/observation**, document analysis.
**FR** = *what* the system does (a service/feature). **NFR** = *how well* / a constraint (performance, reliability, security, usability). One failed NFR can break the whole system.
**Product** (runtime: performance, dependability, security, usability), **Organisational** (org policy: e.g. 'must use Java'), **External** (regulatory, ethical, legislative — e.g. GDPR).

**Confidentiality** (disclosure only to authorised), **Integrity** (no unauthorised modification), **Availability** (accessible when needed). Often extended with authentication, authorisation, non-repudiation.
**SMART** (good *requirements*): Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. **INVEST** is for *user stories*. Don't swap them!

cards.front: SRS — what it is + IEEE standard
cards.back: **Software Requirements Specification** = the agreed **contract** stating *what* to implement (says what, not how). Follows **IEEE 830**. Should be complete, consistent, unambiguous, verifiable, traceable.
Table mapping each **requirement → design → code → test cases** (forward) and back. Proves **coverage**, enables **change-impact analysis**, catches gold-plating.
**Structural** (static): class, object, component, deployment, package. **Behavioural** (dynamic): use-case, sequence, activity, state-machine, communication, timing.
**«include»** = base **always** uses it (mandatory, shared behaviour). **«extend»** = **optional/conditional** behaviour added at an extension point. Mnemonic: include='always', extend='sometimes'.
**Main/basic flow** = happy path. **Alternative flow** = valid variation. **Exception flow** = error path. Actor = a **role** (human or another system), external to the system.

**Persona** = a fictional, research-based archetype of a user type (goals, frustrations, context) — fights the 'elastic user'. **Scenario** = a narrative story of a persona using the system to reach a goal.

Passive observation of real work → uncovers **tacit requirements** users never state. **Flipkart**: observing distrust of online payment + poor connectivity drove **Cash-on-Delivery** and low-data UIs.
**Verification** = 'building the product **right**' (conforms to spec; often static/reviews). **Validation** = 'building the **right** product' (meets user needs; often dynamic).
A human makes an **error (mistake)** → introduces a **defect/fault (bug)** in the code → which, when executed, may cause a **failure** at runtime. A defect doesn't always cause a failure.
**Unit** (one component) → **Integration** (interfaces between modules) → **System** (whole integrated system vs requirements) → **Acceptance** (vs customer needs; alpha/beta/UAT).
**Black-box** = test against the **spec** (inputs→expected outputs), no code view — e.g. boundary-value analysis. **White-box** = test internal **logic/paths** — e.g. branch coverage.
ID, description, preconditions, **inputs/steps**, **expected result (oracle)**, actual result, status. Without a predefined **expected result** you can't tell pass from fail.
Scope/approach, **features to be tested + NOT tested**, **item pass/fail criteria**, **suspension/resumption criteria**, deliverables, environment, schedule, risks. Defines what/how/who/when.
Statement < branch/decision < path coverage (strength). **100% statement coverage ≠ bug-free** — it shows what ran, not whether outputs are correct or code is missing.

**Defect density = defects ÷ size (KLOC / FP)** — normalises quality across modules. **Security validation** adds misuse cases, **pen-testing**, vulnerability scanning, **fuzzing** on top of normal V&V.
